title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: A machine sale is a one-time transaction; a machine working two shifts a day in abrasive rock is a ten-year annuity in wear parts.
epigraph.author: Heavy Equipment Economics

web_blocks.html: Under Ind AS 108, Eimco Elecon reports one primary operating segment: Machinery and Spares. It engineers, fabricates, and assembles its full product range at its Vallabh Vidyanagar plant in Gujarat. In practice, however, the company runs on three distinct revenue engines. Those three engines are (1) Underground Mining Equipment (Coal & Metal), (2) After-Sales Spares & Lifecycle Services, and (3) Construction & Foundation Equipment.

web_blocks.html: Concrete Real-World Example 1: The Blast-Free Continuous Miner Package in an Underground Coal Mine. Picture a private Mine Developer-cum-Operator (MDO) hired by Coal India to reopen a closed underground coal seam in Chhattisgarh. In the past, the mine used drill-and-blast methods with Eimco Elecon 625 SDLs loading blasted coal onto conveyors, which was slow and labour-heavy. Today, Eimco Elecon supplies a complete, homegrown Continuous Miner package. The CM3500 Continuous Miner cuts coal straight from the seam face without explosives using rotating cutter drums. An Eimco Elecon 10-tonne Shuttle Car carries the cut coal to a Feeder Breaker that crushes lumps onto the main belt conveyor. Meanwhile, a Twin-Boom Roof Bolter (TRS) secures the newly exposed mine roof right behind the cut. To move crews through low 1.35m–1.5m seams without diesel fumes, the mine can add Eimco's flameproof, battery-powered MCAR-E (14+1 personnel carrier) and UV-A-BE (10-tonne utility vehicle). Over a 9-year machine life, every shift wears down cutter bits, hydraulic hoses, conveyor chains, and gearbox seals, creating steady spares orders for Eimco Elecon's Bilaspur depot.

Concrete Real-World Example 2: Hard-Rock Piling for Metro & Highway Foundations. Outside coal, consider an infrastructure contractor building elevated metro piers or bridge abutments in hard rock. Imported European piling rigs from Bauer, Soilmec, or Liebherr carry high upfront prices and long wait times for spare parts. Eimco Elecon builds the EC216 / EC267 Piling Rig in Vallabh Vidyanagar on a Hitachi base carrier using CZM (USA) technology. Each rig features Hardox-steel Kelly bars, an anti-shock valve for hard rock, and a MOBA digital system that logs real-time torque and depth. In October 2026, Eimco Elecon widened this foundation line by launching the homegrown DW-220 Hydraulic Diaphragm Wall Grab for deep urban basements, metro stations, and dam cut-off walls.

Spare-Parts Lifecycle Economics & Fleet Annuity Mechanics: Eimco Elecon does not split out equipment and spares revenue in its quarterly filings. Still, its active fleet of 1,065 machines—with 683 coal units (64.1%) and 382 non-coal metal and mineral units (35.9%)—anchors the business. Underground loaders and Continuous Miners run two or three shifts a day in wet, abrasive, and acidic rock. Over a 7-to-9-year working life, a heavy LHD or Continuous Miner package consumes wear parts, hydraulic cylinders, crawler tracks, cutter picks, gearboxes, and electrical assemblies. That cumulative spares spend often equals or exceeds the machine's original purchase price. Coal India, SCCL, and private MDOs face heavy output penalties if a face loader stalls. As a result, getting spares within 24–48 hours matters far more to a mine manager than a small discount on upfront capex. That field reality supports Eimco Elecon's 10 regional depots and cushions margins whenever new-machine tenders slow down.

Electrification, Metal Mining & Import-Substitution Piling Rigs: Beyond coal, Eimco Elecon aims its R&D at two growing adjacencies. First, in April 2026, it launched the flameproof, battery-powered MCAR-E (1.35m height, 14+1 seats) and UV-A-BE (1.5m height, 10-tonne payload, Degree-1 gassy mine certified). These vehicles target India's 8.56% CAGR battery-electric mining shift by cutting diesel exhaust heat and ventilation costs for Hindustan Zinc, Hindustan Copper, and CIL. Second, VP Amit Kumar noted in an October 2026 NBM&CW interview that Eimco Elecon is India's sole multi-size domestic maker of hydraulic piling rigs (EC125, EC216, EC267). Built on Hitachi base platforms with CZM (USA) tech and MOBA monitoring, these rigs were joined in October 2026 by the DW-220 Hydraulic Diaphragm Wall Grab. Local fabrication and fast hydraulic support help Eimco win Make-in-India infrastructure tenders against European imports, though its articulated wheel loaders still face tough Chinese price competition.

Segment Economics Comparison — Coal vs. Metal vs. Foundation Rigs: Each of Eimco Elecon's three verticals carries a different ticket size and margin profile. Standalone coal loaders (SDLs and LHDs) are mature, high-share products with steady spares pull-through across 683 active coal machines. By contrast, a full Continuous Miner package (CM3500, shuttle cars, roof bolter, feeder breaker) is a multi-crore system sale. Commissioning a CM package creates sharp quarterly revenue spikes and locks in high-value cutter-drum and pick replacements. In non-coal metal mining (382 active units at Hindustan Zinc, Hindustan Copper, and UCIL), 7-tonne and 10-tonne LHDs compete directly with Sandvik and Epiroc on uptime. Finally, EC-series piling rigs and the DW-220 diaphragm wall grab serve urban metro and bridge projects, where fast local service offsets European brand prestige.

web_blocks.title: The Hidden Concentration & Chinese Price-Pressure Reality
paragraphs: Even with piling rigs and metal-mine sales, CRISIL's August 2026 review confirms that 75–80% of Eimco Elecon's revenue still comes from underground mining. That share is down from over 90% before 2022, yet coal mining remains the dominant driver.

In construction wheel loaders (2.3T and 3.5T), management notes fierce price pressure from Chinese OEMs such as Sany, XCMG, and LiuGong. That rivalry limits pricing power outside specialized piling rigs.

book_paragraphs: On paper, Eimco Elecon's financial statements look deceptively simple: under Ind AS 108, the company reports just one accounting segment called 'Machinery and Spares.' But if you and I stopped at that single line, we would miss the three very different economic engines humming inside the Vallabh Vidyanagar factory—and we would misjudge both the durability of its core franchise and the competitive friction in its newer product lines.

The first and largest engine—still accounting for roughly 75% to 80% of total revenue when you include spares, according to CRISIL's August 2026 review—is underground mining equipment. Eimco Elecon is the dominant domestic supplier of the workhorse machines that load roughly 65% to 70% of India's intermediate underground coal: Side Dump Loaders in the 611, 625, and 635 series, Load Haul Dumpers in the 811 and 912 series, Universal Drill Machines, and Chairlift Man-Riding Systems. Over the last few years, the company has graduated from selling standalone loaders to delivering a complete, 100% indigenized blast-free Continuous Miner package—combining the CM3500 cutter, 10-tonne shuttle cars, twin-boom roof bolters, and feeder breakers—alongside two flameproof battery-electric underground vehicles, the MCAR-E and UV-A-BE, launched in April 2026.

The second engine is the aftermarket annuity. Out of 1,065 active Eimco Elecon machines currently working underground—683 in coal mines and 382 in non-coal metal and mineral mines operated by Hindustan Zinc, Hindustan Copper, and Uranium Corporation of India—every machine grinds through hydraulic seals, cutter picks, conveyor chains, and undercarriage components two shifts a day. Regional depots in Asansol, Dhanbad, Bilaspur, Nagpur, and Jamshedpur keep those parts within hours of the mine portal, turning one-time machine deliveries into multi-year, higher-margin spare parts streams.

book_subsections.title: Walking Through a Chhattisgarh Coal Face and a Metro Piling Site
paragraphs: To see how these machines work together in the real world, picture you and I descending into a deep coal seam in Chhattisgarh operated by a private Mine Developer-cum-Operator under a Coal India contract. Twenty years ago, miners drilled holes into the coal wall, packed them with explosives, evacuated the gallery, blasted the seam, and waited for toxic fumes to clear before an Eimco 625 Side Dump Loader could scoop up the broken coal. Today, the operator deploys Eimco Elecon's CM3500 Continuous Miner: its rotating cutter drum shears coal directly from the face without a single stick of explosive. An Eimco 10-tonne Shuttle Car shuttles the cut coal to a Feeder Breaker that crushes lumps onto the main belt conveyor, while a Twin-Boom Roof Bolter secures the freshly exposed ceiling immediately behind the cut. To ferry crews through tight 1.35-metre seams without adding diesel exhaust heat, the mine pairs the fleet with the battery-electric MCAR-E personnel carrier and UV-A-BE utility vehicle. Over a nine-year lifecycle, every shift generates recurring orders for wear parts from the Bilaspur depot.

Now let us ride the cage back up to the surface and visit an elevated metro-rail or highway bridge construction site. Here, Eimco Elecon's third engine—Construction and Foundation Equipment—puts its CZM-collaborated EC125, EC216, and EC267 hydraulic piling rigs and its October 2026 DW-220 Diaphragm Wall Grab to work. Built on Hitachi base carriers with Hardox-steel Kelly bars, anti-shock valves for hard Indian rock, and MOBA digital depth monitoring, these rigs bore deep cast-in-place foundation piles while logging real-time torque. As VP Amit Kumar highlighted in an October 2026 industry interview, Eimco Elecon is India's sole multi-size domestic piling rig manufacturer, giving contractors a 'Make in India' alternative to expensive European imports like Bauer and Soilmec—though management candidly admits its conventional 2.3-tonne and 3.5-tonne articulated wheel loaders face brutal price competition from Chinese OEMs like Sany, XCMG, and LiuGong.

book_subsections.title: Why Wear Parts Turn One Machine Sale Into a Nine-Year Relationship
paragraphs: If you have never stood beside an underground coal loader after a single eight-hour shift, it is hard to appreciate how violently rock destroys steel. An Eimco Side Dump Loader or Load Haul Dumper spends its working life ramming its bucket into jagged, blasted coal and shale, pivoting on wet mine floors, and hauling multi-tonne loads through cramped galleries. Hydraulic hoses abrade against tunnel walls, undercarriage pins grind down in coal dust, and Continuous Miner cutter picks blunt against stone bands.

That harsh physical reality is the secret behind Eimco Elecon's second economic engine: the aftermarket. With 1,065 active machines operating across India—683 in coal mines and 382 in non-coal metal and mineral mines—Eimco Elecon does not just sell a piece of iron and walk away. Over a machine's seven-to-nine-year operational life, the mine operator repeatedly buys replacement hydraulic cylinders, seal kits, gearboxes, crawler chains, and cutter bits. Because an idle loader at the coal face costs a mine far more in lost output than the price of a spare part, colliery engineers overwhelmingly prefer OEM-certified components stocked nearby.

That is why Eimco Elecon maintains 10 regional sales and service depots in hubs like Dhanbad, Asansol, Bilaspur, Nagpur, Jamshedpur, and Secunderabad. And notice how the April 2026 launch of the battery-electric MCAR-E and UV-A-BE extends that razor-and-blade model: as underground mines electrify to cut diesel fumes and cooling costs, Eimco Elecon is positioning itself to own the next generation of flameproof battery packs, drivetrains, and specialized service contracts.

book_subsections.title: Evaluating Product Quality: From Conventional Loaders to Digital Piling Rigs
paragraphs: You might wonder how a single 15-acre plant in Gujarat manages to build machines as different as a 1.35-metre-tall underground coal personnel carrier and a towering hydraulic piling rig. The secret lies in shared heavy-fabrication and hydraulic-integration capabilities. Whether a machine is boring a thirty-metre foundation pile for an urban metro pier or loading blasted zinc ore a kilometre underground, the core engineering challenges are identical: high-torque hydraulic circuits, stress-relieved structural steel booms, reliable powertrains, and ruggedized electronic monitoring.

Listen to how VP Amit Kumar described the piling-rig strategy in his October 2026 NBM&CW interview: by pairing a proven Hitachi base carrier with CZM's American foundation-drilling technology, Hardox-steel Kelly bars, an anti-shock valve for hard rock, and MOBA digital depth monitoring, Eimco Elecon created a machine engineered specifically for Indian geological strata rather than importing a European rig priced for Western labour rates. And with the October 2026 launch of the DW-220 Hydraulic Diaphragm Wall Grab, the company is widening its infrastructure footprint into deep urban basements and dam cut-off walls—giving it a second growth leg that does not depend on Coal India's tender calendar.

Notice also how Eimco Elecon protects itself from single-product obsolescence across those three engines. When underground coal mines relied primarily on drill-and-blast loading, Side Dump Loaders and Load Haul Dumpers carried the entire franchise. As Coal India and private Mine Developer-cum-Operators shifted toward higher-output Continuous Miner galleries, Eimco Elecon engineered the CM3500 package, shuttle cars, roof bolters, and feeder breakers to capture the higher ticket size. And as infrastructure EPC contractors demanded domestic alternatives to imported foundation rigs, the Vallabh Vidyanagar team adapted its heavy-fabrication and hydraulic skills into EC-series piling rigs and the DW-220 diaphragm wall grab. Each step built on the same manufacturing backbone rather than chasing unrelated businesses.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Razor-and-Blade Ratio to Watch
book_callouts.text: Eimco Elecon does not publicly break out exact equipment versus spares revenue in its quarterly presentations. When you and I read management commentary, we should always track active fleet growth—currently 1,065 machines—and inventory composition, because a growing installed base is what cushions margins when new-machine tenders pause.
